 Since coming back to beat Roma in mid-October, Madrid has raised its attacking output, averaging more than three goals per game.
 Mario de la Riva twitter William Allen Update: Nov 5th, 2026 03:17 EST 0 Share facebook twitter whatsapp Make us preferred on Google Speaking ahead of yesterday’s game in Athens, Real Madrid boss José Mourinho was reluctant to describe the team’s comeback win in Rome as a turning point. But the numbers tell a different story . It was the first time Madrid had overturned a deficit this season, a feat they repeated against AEK . And between those two games, the team has become an attacking juggernaut. Madrid has scored 20 goals in six matches, averaging more than three per game. While the Madrid coach preferred to downplay any dramatic shift, the reality is that the team has found another gear offensively since that victory.
 “From an emotional standpoint, of course it has an impact,” Mourinho said of Madrid’s 4-3 victory over Roma. “You’re losing a game that looks gone, and then you come back and win it. Naturally, that can always leave you with something positive emotionally. But as a ‘turning point’ in terms of our play? I don’t think so. I believe more in the process than in a specific moment . We understand each other better every day.”
 A Real difference in front of goal
 Madrid has gone from averaging 2.3 goals per game against its first nine opponents this season, to 3.3 goals per game over its last six outings . The match in Athens was the game in which Mourinho’s side produced the most shots all season. They attempted 24, matching their total against Rayo Vallecano. The difference has been efficiency. Madrid has averaged 17.6 shots per game across both stretches of the season, from the opening weeks through Villarreal and from Athens through Rome. What has changed is the conversion rate: earlier in the campaign, Madrid needed seven shots to score; now it needs barely more than five.
 Real Madrid Spain
 News 
 Statistics 
 Advanced metrics also highlight that improvement through expected goals (xG) , a statistic that estimates how many goals a player or team should score on average based on the quality of the chances created. For every shot, xG evaluates the likelihood of scoring using factors such as the type of assist, the angle of the attempt, and the distance from goal. Until the Villarreal match, Madrid had scored 1.69 fewer goals than expected. The clearest example was against Real Betis. The only game in which Mourinho’s side failed to score was also the one in which it posted its highest expected-goals total: 3.46. 
 Over the last six matches, by contrast, Madrid has scored 4.5 goals more than expected . And that figure could have been even higher, considering the team underperformed its xG in each of the last two games. In Santander, Madrid generated 3.36 xG. The numbers said it, and so did Mourinho. “In my opinion, the team should have scored more goals from the chances we created,” he lamented at El Sardinero. Then in Athens, Madrid posted 3.35 xG. Against AEK, the Spanish giants registered 24 shots in total, nine of them from Kylian Mbappé, with eight efforts on target and another strike from Mbappé rattling the woodwork.

 Mbappé on the mark
 The French superstar has been ever-present on the scoresheet during this six-game stretch. Mbappé produced braces in both El Clásico and against Sevilla, while also finding the net against Roma, RB Leipzig, Racing, and AEK. In his last two appearances he also struck the post once in each match, and he added an assist against Leipzig. Yan Diomande, Jude Bellingham, and Arda Güler have been particularly influential as well. The Ivorian has contributed three goals and three assists. The Englishman has scored in each of the last two matches and set up Mbappé against Sevilla. Meanwhile, the Turkish playmaker, who was rested and did not travel to Athens, has two goals and three assists in his last five games. Carlos Espí, Endrick, Antonio Rüdiger, Bernardo Silva, and Fede Valverde round out the list of scorers during a six-game run in which Madrid has reignited its firepower.
